documentation.content:
A channel that a live source token makes expected has gone a working day (a week for the cloud hook, two days for a reconciler) without a row. The gauge is one `skill platform summary` line per (platform, environment, origin) computed from the newest row of `skill_invocations` under that platform and environment, never per token, with Saturday 00:00 to Monday 00:00 in the mask zone (America/New_York in server/store/skills.go) not counted; a series whose token never posted reads the sentinel 100000, so a beacon that never worked alerts too. The `laptop` environment is not here (each per-person token is its own series and the token summary covers it) and neither is `canary` (a token minted to prove the gauge and post nothing), nor Vorflux, whose beacon is optional.

Which series: `gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="loop-sessions" AND jsonPayload.message="skill platform summary"' --freshness=10m --format='value(jsonPayload.platform,jsonPayload.environment,jsonPayload.origin,jsonPayload.minutes_since_last_row,jsonPayload.rows_24h)'`, then the token: `last_used_minutes_ago` on the `skill token summary` line for that platform and environment. A token used recently with no rows is the emitter posting and being refused (policies 17, 17b, 17e say why); a token not used at all is the vendor secret missing or stale, the mirror no longer carrying the beacon line, `rate_limit_per_min` at 0 from an unfinished rotation, or the platform's egress. A silent reconciler is the automation stopped: re-enable it or restart the monitor. A platform that has genuinely stopped using skills is not an incident: revoke its token so the series stops being expected.

Runbook: examples/deploy-gcp/README.md#runbook-source-tokens
